bundle.note: The enrollment bundle (identity-enrollment.md §5.4): an unsigned CBOR map carrying the device_cert and card above. Unsigned because both members are signed already; what has to be checked is that the card belongs to the identity the certificate names, which it does here.

fields.attestations: [the signed attestation above, embedded as a map]
fields.name: Alice

card_successor.note: A card that pre-commits a successor identity (§3.4). A server that has cached this card must refuse a later card for the same identity carrying a different successor, or none.

enroll_request.note: A renewal request (identity-enrollment.md §4, §8) that also carries a `pair` tag from the QR path (§5.6), so one vector exercises every field. `prev` is the device_cert above, and names the same device as this request; `pair` is HMAC-SHA-256(pairing_secret, device). Signed by the *device* key, not the identity key — the object names the only key that could have signed it.

enroll_session_claim.note: A holder proving to a mailbox that it holds the identity key whose renewals it is asking to stand by for (identity-enrollment.md §5.1). Signed by the *identity* key, unlike the enroll_request above. `session` is SHA-256 of `session_secret`, the secret the mailbox handed the holder when it opened the session, so a captured claim is worth nothing against any other session; the secret is published here only so the hash can be rechecked.

freeze.note: Signed by keys.registrar. `frozen` is CBOR true (0xf5).

notes: All byte strings are lowercase hex.
Seeds are the 32-byte Ed25519 private key seeds (RFC 8032). Device X25519 secret = SHA-256("hl-identity/device-enc/v1" || seed).
signature_input_hex = domain || 0x00 || unsigned_hex; signature_hex = Ed25519(seed, signature_input).
signed_hex is the deterministic CBOR of the unsigned map plus a `sig` entry, keys sorted by encoded bytes.
Fingerprint = SHA-256(public key), shown as lowercase Crockford base32, 52 digits.
`rejects` entries must fail to parse with the named error; implementations that don't distinguish error kinds should at least fail.
`pair` = HMAC-SHA-256(key = pairing_secret, message = device public key), 32 bytes.
The bundle is the one object here with no signature of its own; `encoded_hex` rather than `signed_hex` says so.

Registrar objects (identity-registrar.md §4) sign like every other. The rotation has a second signature: ack_input_hex = domain || "/ack" || 0x00 || unsigned_hex, where unsigned_hex is the map without `sig` *and* `ack`; ack_hex is Ed25519(successor seed, ack_input).
A record list's `entries` are [seq, bytes] pairs; each bytes is a record with its own signature, verified on its own. Its `fingerprint` is SHA-256 of the key the list was asked for.

records.note: keys.identity's per-identity list, signed by keys.registrar. `fingerprint` is the one the list was asked for; `entries` are [seq, record bytes], each record the vector of the same name. Seq 3 is another identity's record and is not in this list.

records_empty.note: An empty per-identity list: the registrar holds nothing against keys.other. Signed, so a cache can hold it.

register.note: A first registration: an invite as `proof`, and a `successor` commitment to keys.successor.

register_reissue.note: A reissue: the same handle, no proof, the same commitment — dropping it would be refused.

rejects.name: duplicate map key, otherwise in canonical order
map keys out of canonical order
more attestations than a card may carry
device revocation signed by a device whose certificate lacks manage
rotation acknowledged by a key other than the successor

revoke_attestation.note: Signed by keys.registrar: every attestation of alice@hl.example to keys.identity issued at or before `time` is void.

revoke_device.note: Signed by the identity key. `device` is keys.lost_device.

revoke_device_by_device.note: Signed by keys.device, carrying its own certificate as `signer_cert`: unrestricted caps, so `manage`. The signature is by `signer`, not the identity.

rotate.note: `sig` by the predecessor (keys.identity) and `ack` by the successor (keys.successor), both over unsigned_hex — the map without `sig` and `ack` — under the domain and the domain with `/ack` appended.
